summary: Model picker is the control a person uses to choose which model answers in a chat, and how hard it thinks first. Each model shows its speed, quality and cost as five-step meters with the real figures on hover, the thinking effort sits underneath, and the foot of the list says what the next reply will take. When the picked model can't take the request, the picker says why and offers a way out.
use: When people choose between models that trade speed, quality and cost, and should see those trade-offs before they pick.
When a model can think before it answers and people should set how much, with an idea of what it costs in time and money.
When a model can be at capacity or unavailable, and you want to offer a wait or a close match instead of an error.
When the choice applies to one chat and people need a quiet confirmation of what is set.
features: Each model row has a coloured tile, a name, a one-line `note`, and three five-step meters for `speed`, `quality` and `cost`. `speedDetail`, `qualityDetail` and `costDetail` show on hover, like "74 tokens a second".
The picked row is tinted and checked, and its meters turn the accent colour. The trigger above the list shows the picked model and effort, and both crossfade when they change.
A model's `status` can be `checking`, which spins beside its name, or `busy`, which turns its tile and line amber. `statusText` replaces the note, like "At capacity, about 20s wait".
`suggestion` opens a short message under the list with its buttons, the last one filled, like Wait for Opus and Use Sonnet on high. It opens and closes by its height.
The thinking effort is a segmented control. `efforts` defaults to Off, Low, Medium and High, each with a line shown under "Thinking", like "Up to 8k thinking tokens".
`estimate` fills the foot of the list, and `note` adds a confirmation with a green check under the picker. The trigger opens and closes the list.
a11y: The models form a radio group labelled "Model". Each row is a button with `role="radio"` and `aria-checked`, and only the picked one is in the tab order.
Arrow keys move to the next or previous model and pick it, wrapping at the ends.
The trigger has `aria-expanded`. Escape closes the list and moves the focus back to the trigger.
The thinking effort is a group labelled "Thinking effort" whose buttons use `aria-pressed`, and the suggestion and the confirmation are live regions.

faq.q: Does it check whether a model is available?
faq.a: No. It calls `onValueChange` with the id of any row that is picked, busy or not. Check the model in your own code, set its `status` to `checking` and then `busy` or `ready`, and pass a `suggestion` if it can't start.

faq.q: Where do the meters and the estimate come from?
faq.a: From you. Give each model `speed`, `quality` and `cost` from 1 to 5, and the figures behind them in the detail props. `estimate` is any content, so you can work out the next reply's time and price however your provider charges.

faq.q: Can I use my own effort levels?
faq.a: Yes. Pass `efforts` as a list of `{ label, detail }`. The picked one is `effort` or `defaultEffort`, which defaults to the third in the list, or the last if there are fewer.
Yes. It opens by default; set `defaultOpen={false}`, or control it with `open` and `onOpenChange`.
